title: Narration written for the ear
statement: Write narration for the ear: introduce a shorthand once and then say it in full, because a repeated bare abbreviation is read aloud as a string of letters.
example: One automated check flags a token of 2 to 5 capital letters used at least twice and never expanded.
detail: The video-script tools adopt the convention from an internal instruction guide: narration is read aloud, so a domain shorthand should be introduced once and then spoken in full, since bare repeated acronyms come out as robotic letter strings (`shadow-bench`, git commit 0250c70). A lint flags a token of 2–5 uppercase letters that is not a normally spoken acronym, is never expanded in the script, and is used at least twice.
against: 'Report-only by design — acronym heuristics are noisy, so this advises generators rather than failing scripts.' (`shadow-bench`, git commit 0250c70, lines 17-18).

evidence.quote: Narration is read aloud (Generic §18): a domain shorthand ("MB") should be introduced once and thereafter spoken in full — bare repeated acronyms read as robotic letter-strings.

Adds a high-precision, report-only lint that flags a token only when it is 2–5 uppercase letters, not a normally-spoken acronym (DNA/GDP/…), not expanded anywhere in the script, and used at least twice.
Report-only by design — acronym heuristics are noisy, so this advises generators rather than failing scripts.
the SPOKEN strings never say "the So row" — TTS elides it.
